newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee fails to shine despite NY rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee fails to shine despite NY rally.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures maintained slight losses by the close on Monday, ignoring a new rally in New York on local and fund buying.
Traders said London's failure to make any breakthrough on the upside reflected the persistent lack of buying power.
"At the moment, it doesn't seem wanting to break on the upside," said one trader. "It could move lower to $1,500 initially basis May, then the $1,420-$1,380 chart gap."
The May position, London's benchmark, traded from $1,540 and $1,564 a tonne to end the day $5 down at $1,559.
July was also $7 lower at $1,565. It was the most active contract as some players rolled out of the May positions ahead of the first delivery day on May 1.
London continued to trail New York as the arabica futures headed sharply higher after a rise to 192 cents a lb basis May triggered local buying.
One London trader said fund buying was also seen in New York.
Others said a cocktail of recent labour problems in Colombia and Brazil and the continued fall in U.S. certified stocks could have contributed to the bullish direction.
May/May arbitrage against New York still stood at a wide 122 cents and July/July at 103 cents.
In London, there were no signs of fund buying. Even roaster activity has come down to a trickle.
Robustas are still well-supplied and the market is now bracing for what some traders said earlier-than-usual Indonesia's main harvest.
Immediately, the market is waiting for U.S. March green coffee stocks due after the close of New York trading on Tuesday to give further direction.

Coffee fell sharply last week on talk of a 1.0-million bag rise in the March inventory. Traders now thought the data could show an increase of 250,000 to 350,000 bags from February's 1.54 million. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
